Proven by failing-first doc_open refusal pins (fresh-open None, fresh-open-after-close Some(inactive), resync restoration, epoch non-reuse, 200 success control), failing-first endpoint publish pins (transient success, exhaustion, first-attempt control) driven by the injected writer, failing-first invoke body-bound and renderer-withholding pins, and the unchanged predecessor suites named by the spec with zero moved pins.

(3) The refusal branch sits after the budget checks (1475-1512) so it can neither relax nor re-order them; the budget contract "a refusal leaves it untouched" (250-253) holds because the refused session and its fresh budget are discarded whole. (4) The emit-failure seam is cfg(test)-gated and lives in live_bridge.rs: the DOC_OPEN_EMIT_INJECTION AtomicBool consulted only by emit_doc_open, armed via the cfg(test) helper arm_doc_open_emit_injection(armed: bool); emit_live_update, emit_doc_patch, emit_doc_close and emit_context_request stay byte-identical, so the single emit point and the mid-stream log-only behavior are preserved; release builds compile the seam out and the main.rs literal (823-828) stays textually unchanged. (5) Endpoint publication: pub fn publish_endpoint_with_retry(endpoint, writer) -> EndpointPublication {Published, PublishedAfterRetry { attempt }, Unpublished { attempts }} in live_endpoint.rs beside the endpoint file I/O, with named constants ENDPOINT_PUBLISH_ATTEMPTS (3) and ENDPOINT_PUBLISH_RETRY_PAUSE_MS (250) — a bounded total window well under a second, std::thread::sleep pauses, startup-only, no timer/queue/watcher infrastructure; each failed attempt keeps the BLOCK_ENDPOINT_WRITE_FAILED name with an attempt={n}/{N} counter, each pause logs BLOCK_ENDPOINT_PUBLISH_RETRY, exhaustion logs BLOCK_ENDPOINT_UNPUBLISHED port={} attempts={} — the "live server running but its address is unpublished after N attempts" state, textually and semantically distinct from BLOCK_START_FAILED's "no server"; main.rs passes the real m045_ext::write_endpoint as the writer; a first-attempt success writes exactly once with the existing BLOCK_WRITE_OK and the returned Published outcome; cleanup_endpoint, check_stale and the stale-PID logic are untouched. (6) Invoke bounds: INVOKE_MESSAGE_MAX_CHARS = 400 (a few hundred characters); fn sanitize_foreign_body neutralizes every C0/C1 control character and DEL to U+FFFD and, past the body's share of the bound, appends fn truncation_marker's "[truncated: {original_bytes} bytes withheld]" naming the ORIGINAL size; fn bound_message clamps EVERY InvokeError.message under the same constant at all six construction sites so parse-failure and client-build messages stay bounded too; InvokeError gains http_status: Option<u16> (None for non-HTTP classes; Display unchanged mechanically) so mod.rs mt_ext_invoke renders BadStatus as the class, the HTTP status and "extension response body withheld" without any body fragment, while non-BadStatus command errors keep format!("{e}") (bounded, no foreign body involved); BLOCK_INVOKE_FAILED keeps logging reason={e} — the journal keeps the bounded, sanitized, marker-carrying text and the renderer loses the foreign material entirely; no content-level redaction or secret scanning is attempted. T-002.Title: Honest open: the handle_doc_open emit-failure rollback and refusal in live_server

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src-tauri/src/m045_ext/live_server.rs handle_doc_open becomes honest on delivery: immediately after the enabled re-check and BEFORE decide_open (i.e. before any classification or mutation) it captures the pre-open guard value (let pre_open = session_guard.clone(); — the exact Option<LiveSession>); the emit leg (currently 1540-1550) changes so an emission failure logs the distinct BLOCK_DOC_OPEN_DELIVERY_REFUSED marker carrying session_id and reason={e} but no document content, restores the captured value verbatim (*session_guard = pre_open;), and returns (DOC_OPEN_DELIVERY_REFUSED_STATUS, Json(json!({"error": "live document delivery failed"}))) where DOC_OPEN_DELIVERY_REFUSED_STATUS is a named 500-class StatusCode constant (INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, the file's pairing-state-unavailable/channel-closed precedents). The refusal never prints BLOCK_DOC_OPEN_OK and never answers accepted:true; a successful emission keeps the path from the OK log (1552-1555) through the 200 answer (1557-1563) byte-identical.

The rollback semantics are exact-value, not shape-based: a plain fresh open rolls back to None; a fresh open after a close or a heartbeat-timeout close rolls back to Some(the inactive pre-open session with its original id and epoch); a ReplaceSameSession resync rolls back to the replaced session whole (epoch, document_md, sections, revision, budget). The refusal branch sits after the budget checks (1475-1512) so it can neither relax nor re-order them, charges no budget (the refused session and its fresh StreamBudget are discarded whole — the 250-253 "a refusal leaves it untouched" contract holds), runs entirely in-memory under the already-held stream_gate and session lock (no lock-order change, no native I/O), and never decrements or resets next_epoch — a consumed epoch stays consumed and a later successful open carries a strictly higher epoch.

The refusal is additive to the response vocabulary: the C-STREAM-BUDGET 413/429 refusals, the 401/409 authentication and conflict branches, the DocOpenResponse success shape and every request shape keep their exact statuses and bodies; doc_patch, doc_close and the heartbeat-timeout close keep today's log-only emit-failure behavior byte-for-byte (1789-1801, 1871-1882, 2574-2586) — the open is the delivery gate.
